input.prompt:
Your task per the "spec-bottomup" skill: generate fully-verifiable ACSL annotations for a single C function so Frama-C WP proves the original assertion. Work ONLY inside the given files — do not read anything outside this workspace.

INPUT SLICE (the verification target), stub mode:
"[TASK]/workspace/out/layer0/foo/foo.c"

INLINE REFERENCE (read-only; same code, for understanding):
"[TASK]/workspace/out/layer0/foo/foo.inline.c"

OUTPUT DIR: "[TASK]/workspace/out/layer0/foo/"

Follow spec-bottomup exactly:
1. Read the input slice (and inline ref for understanding).
2. The single function `foo(int n)` has one loop `while (i <= n){ i=i+1; sn=sn+1; }` with pre-state `i=1, sn=0` and `requires 1 <= n;`. Add a full function contract (requires/assigns/ensures) and loop annotations (loop invariant, loop assigns, loop variant) proving `//@ assert(sn == n);` and the post-state.
3. Only ADD ACSL annotations. PRESERVE every original C token — do not change the code. Preserve the original `//@ assert(sn == n);` unchanged and in place.
4. Do NOT use admit, assume, axiom, or external_body.
5. Produce annotated file at:
   "…/out/layer0/foo/foo.acsl.c"
   Use the spectool tool prefix exactly:
   "/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python" -m engine.harness_spectool
   - inject --src <slice.c> --out <foo.acsl.c> --loops '<JSON>'  (or write clusters directly; but never modify the loop/assert code — annotations may only be inserted)
   - verify -f <foo.acsl.c> --timeout 15 --save-stdout <foo.wp.txt>
   - locate-fail --wp <foo.wp.txt> --src <foo.acsl.c>  (iterate up to 5 rounds)
6. Loop analysis facts you may rely on: with `requires 1 <= n`, loop invariant `1 <= i <= n+1` and `sn == i-1` and `sn >= 0` are valid; on exit `i > n` and `i <= n+1` give `i == n+1` hence `sn == n`. Note `sn` is `int`; the iteration count fits in int since i<=n+1 and n is int but n+1 is fine within int for the invariant range given 1<=n. Keep the assertion provable.
7. verify must report Pass (proved == total). Run check-admit -f <foo.acsl.c> to confirm no illegal admits.
8. Return a JSON object on stdout:
{"file":"foo.c","status":"pass"|"fail","round":N,"proved":X,"total":Y,"elapsed_sec":E,"tokens":T,"error":null|"<desc>"}
Only set status "pass" if proved == total and check-admit ok.

Report back the exact content of the final foo.acsl.c file (paste it verbatim) along with the JSON result and wp.txt Pass/Fail lines.
